newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt fund managers remain bullish - MCM survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt fund managers remain bullish - MCM survey.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers kept their bullish sentiment over the past week in the wake of status quo U.S. elections and a steady Federal Reserve monetary policy, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

The catalysts for the bulls were "a steady Fed, no sign of inflation, technical momentum, lack of visible supply and a feeling that election results are a positive at the moment," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 107.7 percent in the week ended November 13 from 107.3 percent in the prior week.

A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk. A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 29 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 24 percent the prior week.
